newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bond prices nudge up, outlook stable.
newsitem.headline: Danish bond prices nudge up, outlook stable.

text.p: Danish bond prices nudged up on Wednesday, aided by greater than expected investor interest with the 10-year yield gap with Germany narrowing and dealers expecting the market to remain stable for the rest of the day.

"It looks like the market will be stable this afternoon. The FOMC meeting, Thursday's Buba session and upcoming US data are expected to put a damper on trade, although no one really expects any US rate adjustments," one dealer said.
The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was up 0.21 point from the opening at 110.71, yielding 6.40 percent in turnover of 965 million crowns.
The 2006 benchmark's March future rose 0.10 point to 110.16 with 47 contracts traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 gained 0.13 point to 87.48.
The crown traded at 3.8148 per mark at 1125 gmt, up marginally from around 3.8152 at the opening.
The 10-year yield gap with Germany narrowed three basis points to 71 during the course of the morning.
The Central Bank was active on the market selling long-term bonds as part of its routine financing operations.
